root.name: Semi-Slav Defense: Anti-Noteboom, Stonewall Variation, Portisch Gambit

overview: In a Stonewall-flavoured Semi-Slav move order Black plays 4...f5, and White offers a pawn with 5.g4, aiming to open the g-file and h-file against Black's king. If Black accepts with 5...fxg4 White has a lead in development and kingside play but is a pawn down; Black can also decline with ...Nf6. The Portisch Gambit is a rare and risky weapon.

white_ideas.idea: Open the kingside with g4 and h3
Develop quickly with Nf3, Bd3 and castle long or short as needed

black_ideas.idea: Accept with ...fxg4 and defend, returning the pawn at the right moment

typical_structures.structure: Stonewall-type pawns with an open g-file after fxg4

character.notes: White's g4 pawn offer makes the position unbalanced and tactical; both kings can be exposed.

gambit.notes: After 5.g4 fxg4 White is a pawn down for open lines; Black can keep it.

soundness.notes: Most strong players regard the sacrifice as unconvincing because Black can hold the pawn and develop.

structure.notes: The f-file and g-file open, the centre stays fluid.

approach.notes: Rarely seen from strong White players.

level.notes: Dubious line needs concrete knowledge but not much theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Declined
sublines_that_differ.how: If Black declines or White captures first, no gambit and a normal Stonewall-type centre results.

character.reason: A flank pawn offer opens the kingside early and gives unbalanced tactical play.

gambit.reason: White plays g4 offering a pawn that Black can keep with ...fxg4.

soundness.reason: Black can accept and develop, and the compensation is hard to prove.

structure.reason: The g and f files open while the centre stays semi-fixed.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose the Portisch Gambit.

level.reason: Dubious so not Beginner; the attacking ideas are simple but trap-heavy.

plans.reason: White's g4 and h-pawn aim directly at the Black king.
